original_question: Let X be a metrizable space. If the Vietoris hyperspace (2^X, T_V) is a Baire space, must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be a Baire space for every metric d compatible with the topology of X?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Question 4.9: whether Baireness of the Vietoris hyperspace implies Baireness of every compatible Wijsman hyperspace on the same metrizable space. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1609.03119))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s exact target: it assumes X is metrizable, takes the hypothesis that the Vietoris hyperspace (2^X, T_V) is Baire, and asks whether the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) must then be Baire for every compatible metric d on X. That is exactly the content of Question 4.9. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1609.03119))
missing_details: State explicitly that 2^X denotes the hyperspace of all non-empty closed subsets of X. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

State explicitly that T_W(d) is the Wijsman topology induced by d, namely the weakest topology on 2^X making all distance functionals d(·,A), A∈2^X, continuous. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

State explicitly that T_V is the Vietoris topology on 2^X; the introduction also records that T_V is the supremum of the Wijsman topologies arising from metrics equivalent to d. ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
For fully stand-alone wording, spell out that a metric d is 'compatible' if it generates the given topology of the metrizable space X. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1609.03119))
If you want paper-faithful metadata, label it as an open question—Question 4.9—rather than as a theorem or conjecture. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1609.03119))
refined_question: Let X be a metrizable space, let 2^X denote the set of all non-empty closed subsets of X, let T_V be the Vietoris topology on 2^X, and for each metric d compatible with the topology of X let T_W(d) denote the Wijsman topology on 2^X induced by d. If (2^X, T_V) is a Baire space, must (2^X, T_W(d)) be a Baire space for every compatible metric d on X? ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))
justification: The draft is targeting the exact item stated as Question 4.9 in Section 4, not a broader neighboring problem such as Problem 4.1 or Question 4.8. Section 1 supplies the hidden notation needed to make the question self-contained: what 2^X means, what T_W(d) means, and how T_V sits relative to compatible Wijsman topologies. The nearby context is Theorem 4.3, which gives a sufficient condition for a positive answer in a different direction—if the countable power X^{aleph_0} is Baire, then (2^X, T_W(d)) is Baire for every compatible metric d—and the author explicitly says he does not know any information toward partial solutions of Questions 4.8 and 4.9. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1609.03119))
